reviews.reason: Both submitted CIFs parse and symmetry-expand as primitive P21/m (No. 11) Ti2Ni2 cells with four fully occupied atoms, the stated 2.73976 x 4.26410 x 4.69024 A, beta = 94.95761 deg cell, sensible complete neighbor shells, and no short contacts; the indexed lattice also accounts well for the principal line positions. The exact atomic realization is nevertheless not established. No comparable whole-pattern score is available, and the trace's 24-group integrated-intensity fit for selected.cif has RMS 0.396 and 13.5% absolute residual without uncertainties or a Pawley/profile lower-bound comparison, including several large weak-line discrepancies. More decisively, the same independent-seed coordinate search in item_48 found an unsubmitted, symmetry-inequivalent full-occupancy P21/m TiNi minimum at Ti (0.290701, 1/4, 0.925027) and Ni (0.714145, 1/4, 0.449670), with objective 5.058 versus 3.770 for the selected model and 5.122 for the submitted literature alternative. It has a chemically valid periodic realization (minimum distance about 2.493 A) and was neither covered nor quantitatively rejected. Another attempt should test and refine this concrete surviving branch with a genuinely comparable whole-profile fit.

Both CIFs parse and primitive-standardize as symmetry-inequivalent P21/m (No. 11) Ti2Ni2 cells with Z=2, four fully occupied sites, the stated 2.73976 x 4.26410 x 4.69024 A, beta=94.95761 deg cell, and chemically plausible complete neighbor shells (minimum periodic distances 2.531 and 2.477 A). Exact recovery is nevertheless not established. The primitive cell leaves reproducible important reflections unexplained, including isolated lines at 40.27, 41.09, 53.03, 69.16, and 82.98 deg at roughly 6-15 times the measured baseline noise, plus the 42.17 deg feature. The trace obtains Rwp=16.61% versus a 14.61% Pawley-like bound only after adding 18 independently fitted nuisance peaks, so this is a flexible composite profile fit rather than an atomic CIF accounting for the full pattern; its RMS residual (0.971) is also about 9.5 times the reported noise (0.102). The trace itself indexed larger monoclinic cells, including a fourfold B19-related cell that places some of these extra lines and an extended cell indexing the first 30 picked lines, but instantiated and refined no corresponding stoichiometric atomic model and did not quantitatively reject symmetry lowering or a superstructure. Another attempt should resolve all significant lines and test an explicit larger-cell/lower-symmetry realization before the submitted primitive models can be accepted as exact.

The submitted CIF is a valid explicit ordered realization: independent parsing and symmetry expansion give primitive P2_1/m (No. 11), Ti2Ni2 (TiNi), Z=2, four fully occupied atoms, and the stated 4.69041 x 4.26412 x 2.73974 A, beta=94.9581 degree cell. Indexing is strong (18/20 initial lines, M(18)=77.4 and F(18)=64.0), and every one of the 22 reflections with prominence >=5 is matched (median position error about 0.006 degree); the isolated unindexed weak features carry only about 0.45% of positive pattern area and define no viable competing cell/model. The trace contains an instantiated 17-90 degree whole-profile coordinate refinement: the selected model's score is 0.01735, versus 0.02996 for swapped Ti/Ni ordering and 0.02077 for the next distinct coordinate minimum; its calculated intensities correlate 0.993 with a free fixed-profile Pawley extraction, with only a modest residual gap (0.182 versus 0.154). A concrete P2_1 symmetry-lowering test minimizes exactly at the submitted mirror coordinate, while a 0.05 fractional displacement worsens the score to 0.03036. The primitive periodic geometry has no overlaps (minimum contact 2.534 A) and complete plausible metallic neighbor shells. Thus ordering and symmetry ambiguities are quantitatively rejected, and no materially different viable branch survives.
